# Block 6: Enforced controls: permissions and detection {.unnumbered} Your instruction fileA file the assistant loads into every conversation, such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, stating the project’s standing conventions. Its contents are requests, not guarantees. and skills are requests: the model usually follows them, but nothing guarantees it. This block shows the controls that *do* hold (raw data untouched, references never regenerated, checks never quietly weakened) and where each one stops. By the end you can check in seconds what your repository prevents and what it detects, which is what lets you hand an agent real work. The same controls protect [Block 7](11g-data-cleaning.qmd) and [Block 9](11i-characterisation-tests.qmd). *⏱ ~30 minutes* ## Layers of control | Layer | Example | What it does | How it fails | |---|---|---|---| | Instruction | `AGENTS.md`, a skill | Requests | Silently ignored | | Approval prompt | "Allow this command?" | Prevents, if you read it | Approval fatigue | | Deny rule | `Edit(/data/raw/**)` | Prevents | Another route reaches the file | | Hook | A script run before each tool call | Prevents | Rephrasing gets past it | | Version control | The Git pane | Detects | Only from your last commit, and only if you look | | Tests and checksums | testthat, `tools::md5sum()` | Detects | Only if they run | Git detects changes only from your last commit, so commit before an agent starts. Your repository's `AGENTS.md` asks the agent to run `git status` before it edits anything, and to stop if there is no repository: a request that helps, but your commit is the control. :::::: {.dia .dia-lanes role="figure" aria-label="Where each control acts. Route 1: the agent asks its edit tool to change a file in data/raw, and the deny rule refuses. Route 2: the agent runs R code that writes the file; with no hook registered, only the approval prompt stands in the way, and if the file changes, git status detects it, as does the checksum test for voles_raw.csv. Instructions and skills are requests that the model may or may not follow."} ::::: {.dia-flow} ::: {.dia-label} Route 1: the agent's edit tool ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-ai} Agent asks to edit `data/raw/scratch.csv` ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} edit tool ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-blocked} Deny rule refuses ::: ::::: ::::: {.dia-flow} ::: {.dia-label} Route 2: R code the agent runs ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-ai} Agent runs `writeLines()` on the same file ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} approval prompt only ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-file} File changed ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} detected by ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-check} `git status` (and, for `voles_raw.csv`, the checksum test) ::: ::::: ::::: {.dia-flow} ::: {.dia-label} Requests, on every route ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-plain} `AGENTS.md` and skills: the model may or may not follow them ::: ::::: ::: {.dia-caption} With no hook registered, only the approval prompt stands between R code and the file. Prevent where you can, detect everywhere. And test every control: one you have not seen refuse something is one you are assuming. ::: :::::: ## Exercise 1: What needs protecting? :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Threat-model your repository (5 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} As a group, fill in the last column: if this went wrong, how would you notice? | Asset | What could go wrong | How you would notice | |---|---|---| | `data/raw/` | Overwritten or "tidied" in place | | | `tests/fixtures/` | The reference regenerated by the code under test | | | `tests/` | A failing test edited until it passes | | | `.claude/`, `.posit/` | The agent's own guardrails switched off | | | `.Renviron`, `.env` | Credentials read and sent to the model provider | | The last two are easy to miss: the files that hold your controls are assets too. **You are done when** every row has an answer. Most will be "the Git pane would show it" or "a test would fail". :::: ::: ## Exercise 2: Deny rules Your workshop repository ships `.claude/settings.json`. It starts the project in **Manual** mode (`default`: asks before every edit and command) and holds 17 deny rulesA permission rule in the deny list of .claude/settings.json that stops Claude Code’s built-in tools from editing or reading the matching files. It checks shell output redirects such as > file, but not R code or most other commands that change the same files. protecting the raw data, the data provider's note, the codebook, the checks, the references, the lockfile and the settings themselves. You never need to edit it: `/permissions` shows the rules and adds new ones. :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## The shipped `.claude/settings.json` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` json { "permissions": { "defaultMode": "default", "deny": [ "Edit(/data/raw/**)", "Read(/docs/data_note.md)", "Edit(/docs/data_note.md)", "Edit(/docs/codebook.csv)", "Edit(/scripts/02_validate.R)", "Edit(/scripts/03_audit_cleaning.R)", "Edit(/scripts/functions/validate_voles.R)", "Edit(/tests/fixtures/**)", "Edit(/tests/make_reference.R)", "Edit(/tests/test_cleaning.R)", "Edit(/renv.lock)", "Edit(/.github/**)", "Edit(/.claude/**)", "Edit(/.posit/**)", "Edit(/hooks/**)", "Read(/.Renviron)", "Read(/.env)" ] } } ``` ::: ::: A leading `/` anchors a pattern to the project root. `Edit` rules cover Claude Code's file-editing tools and shell output redirects (`> file`), not R code it runs, and the documentation does not say they cover `rm`, `mv` or `cp`. The rules protect named files rather than whole folders, so the agent can still write its scripts and tests in Blocks 7 and 9. `Edit(/renv.lock)` keeps `renv::status()` a real check. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Using Posit Assistant Posit Assistant sets permissions per tool in `.posit/assistant/settings.json` (for example `"bash": {"rm *": "deny"}`); `deny` rules hold in every mode, including auto and YOLO. It has no documented path rules for file edits, so rely on the Git pane in step 4. It blocks reading `.env` and `.Renviron` by default. ::: :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Read, test and add a rule, then find the gap (15 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Start state:** your workshop repository open and the Git pane clean. Work on a scratch file, never on real data. **1. Make a scratch file and read the rules.** In the R console: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} writeLines("a", here::here("data", "raw", "scratch.csv")) ``` ::: Commit it in the Git pane. Start `claude` in the Terminal tab and type `/permissions`: the 17 deny rules are listed. **2. See a rule refuse.** **Prompt (Claude Code):** ```text Add a second line, "test", to data/raw/scratch.csv. ``` Notice *who* refuses: | You see | What held | |---|---| | "denied by a permission rule" | The deny rule: enforced, whatever the model intends | | The model declines, citing `AGENTS.md` | Your instruction file: a request that happened to work | If the model declined by itself, reply "This is a scratch file; please make the edit with your edit tool" to see the rule refuse. **3. Add a rule yourself.** In `/permissions`, add `Read(/data/confidential/**)`, one of the confidential-data habits in [Block 4](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd). It applies at once. Then, in the R console: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} testthat::test_file(here::here("tests", "test_controls.R")) ``` ::: The test confirms Manual mode and every shipped rule are still in place. **4. Find the gap.** **Prompt (Claude Code):** ```text Run this R code with Rscript: writeLines(c("a", "test"), "data/raw/scratch.csv") ``` Deny rules do not cover R code, so only the approval prompt stands in the way. **Approve it** (it is a scratch file). The Git pane now shows the file as modified, and **Diff** shows the new line: git caught what no rule prevented. **5. Tidy up.** Revert the file in the Git pane, then delete it and commit the deletion: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} file.remove(here::here("data", "raw", "scratch.csv")) ``` ::: **You are done when** you have seen a rule refuse, added one of your own, seen the Git pane catch the R write, `test_controls.R` passes and `scratch.csv` is gone. **If it goes wrong:** if the model keeps declining in step 4, write the line yourself in the console and carry on: the point is seeing git catch it. If `/permissions` asks where to save your rule, either project file works. :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## At the command line `git add`/`git commit` for step 1, `git diff data/raw` for step 4, and `git restore` then `git rm data/raw/scratch.csv` for step 5. See [checking work](11a-setup-claude-code.qmd#checking-work). ::: :::: ::: A hookA command the assistant runs automatically at a fixed point, for example before every tool call. A hook can block the call, but it matches text, so a differently written command can get past it. is a command the assistant runs before every tool callA single action an agent takes, such as reading a file, editing a file or running a shell command. Permission rules and hooks act on tool calls.. Your instructor may show one; the demonstration is below, and the full hook is in *Going further*. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Instructor: demonstration Your instructor registers a guard hook, written in R, that blocks any call mentioning `data/raw`, and repeats step 4: the hook blocks it before any approval prompt. Then the same write using `here::here("data", "raw", "scratch.csv")`: the text `data/raw` never appears, so the hook lets it through. A text-matching hook is a tripwire, not a wall; the Git pane still shows the change. The full hook is in *Going further*, and the GitHub review gate (CODEOWNERSA GitHub file listing who must review changes to which paths. With branch protection, a pull request that touches those paths cannot merge without their review., branch protectionGitHub repository settings that stop changes reaching a branch such as main unless conditions are met, for example a passing check and an approved review.) is shown in [Block 9](11i-characterisation-tests.qmd). ::: **Your repository now prevents and detects.** The deny rules stop the agent's edit tools touching raw data, the codebook, the checks, the references, the lockfile and the settings. Anything that gets past them by another route is detected: the Git pane shows every changed file, Block 7's checksumA short fingerprint computed from a file’s contents, for example with tools::md5sum(). Any change to the file changes the checksum, so it detects changes made by any route. test fails if the raw data change, and `test_controls.R` fails if a rule disappears or Manual mode is switched off. Protecting something new takes 30 seconds in `/permissions`. For confidential data, add the five habits in [Block 4](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd); and since settings and hooks are code, trust only repositories whose configuration you have read. ::::{.callout-note} ## Set up controls in your own project Your workshop repository came with its controls. A new project of your own starts with none, so set them up before the agent's first task: 1. **Git first.** In the R console, `usethis::use_git()`, and make a first commit. 2. **Add a starter `settings.json`.** Download the one below, save it as `.claude/settings.json`, and edit the paths to match your project. It starts in Manual mode and protects raw data, test references, the lockfile, credentials and itself. Add project-specific rules with `/permissions`. 3. **Ask for git checks.** Copy the *Version control* section of your workshop `AGENTS.md` into your project's instruction file. 4. **Test it.** Ask the agent to edit a protected file and watch the rule refuse; copy `tests/test_controls.R` and change its list of rules to yours. Then commit. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Reference: the starter `settings.json` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` json { "permissions": { "defaultMode": "default", "deny": [ "Edit(/data/raw/**)", "Edit(/tests/fixtures/**)", "Edit(/renv.lock)", "Edit(/.claude/**)", "Read(/.Renviron)", "Read(/.env)" ] } } ``` ::: ::: ::: **Let Claude draft rules, never decide them.** You can ask it to propose deny rules for a project, but read each one: a rule with a wrong path, such as a missing leading `/`, protects nothing and fails silently. Claude Code asks before every write to `.claude/`, and the starter file's `Edit(/.claude/**)` refuses such writes outright, so you install the rules yourself. :::: :::{.callout-note} ## Check · Reproduce · Record - **You can now:** let an agent work in Manual mode in a repository where raw data, references and checks are protected, **trusted because** you have seen a deny rule refuse, seen git catch the route it misses, and have a test that fails if the rules are weakened. - **Check:** watch every control refuse something, and find the route it does not cover. - **Reproduce:** the rules live in `.claude/settings.json`, committed with the project, so everyone who clones it gets the same protection. - **Record:** the Git pane catches a change by any route, counted from your last commit, so commit before the agent starts. Add a line to `docs/ai-log.md` noting which requests were refused. ::: ## Check your understanding **Which control detects a change to raw data made by any route?**
**In Exercise 2, why could the R code change `data/raw/scratch.csv` when the deny rule refused the direct edit?**
**In the demonstration, why did `here::here("data", "raw", "scratch.csv")` get past the guard hook?**
## Going further (not covered live) This material is not covered in the live session. Work through it afterwards if it is useful to you. :::::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## A guard hook A `PreToolUse` hook receives the pending tool call as JSON on standard input (stdin). If it exits with status 2, the call is denied and its message is passed to the model. Claude Code and Posit Assistant use the same shape for this, so one script can serve both. The guard below is written in R. It denies any edit, shell command or R code that mentions a protected path. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} #!/usr/bin/env Rscript # hooks/guard_protected_paths.R ---- # PreToolUse guard for Claude Code and Posit Assistant. # Reads the pending tool call from stdin and exits 2 (deny) if the call # mentions a protected path. A tripwire, not a wall: see "Break your own # guard". protected <- c( "data/raw", "tests/fixtures", "make_reference.R", ".github/workflows" ) payload <- jsonlite::fromJSON( paste(readLines(file("stdin"), warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), simplifyVector = FALSE ) # search the whole tool input as text, so the same rule covers file edits, # shell commands and R code whatever the tool calls its fields call_text <- as.character(jsonlite::toJSON(payload$tool_input, auto_unbox = TRUE)) hits <- protected[vapply(protected, \(p) grepl(p, call_text, fixed = TRUE), logical(1))] if (length(hits) > 0) { message( "Blocked by project guard: this ", payload$tool_name, " call refers to a protected path (", paste(hits, collapse = ", "), "). ", "Do not modify protected files; ask the user to do it." ) quit(save = "no", status = 2) } quit(save = "no", status = 0) ``` ::: The script runs with `Rscript --vanilla`, so it does not start renv, and `jsonlite` must be installed in your user library. **Register it with Claude Code** by adding a `hooks` key to `.claude/settings.json`, alongside the existing `permissions` key. The deny rules protect `.claude/`, so make this edit yourself, not through the agent. ```json { "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Edit|Write|Bash", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "Rscript --vanilla \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/hooks/guard_protected_paths.R" } ] } ] } } ``` The `matcher` lists the tool names the hook runs for. **Register it with Posit Assistant** in `.posit/assistant/settings.json`. The tool names differ: `edit`, `bash`, and `executeR` for R code run in your session. ```json { "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "edit|bash|executeR", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "Rscript --vanilla hooks/guard_protected_paths.R" } ] } ] } } ``` Posit Assistant runs project hooks only in a workspace you have trusted. :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Test the hook before you trust it :::: ::::{.task-container} Hooks fail open. If the script crashes, for example because `jsonlite` is not installed, both tools continue as if the hook had allowed the call. So test the script directly, without the agent. The R below runs the hook exactly as Claude Code does, a fresh `Rscript --vanilla` process given the tool call on standard input, and works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux. **In the R console:** ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} rscript <- file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript") hook <- shQuote(here::here("hooks", "guard_protected_paths.R")) run_hook <- function(json) { system2(rscript, c("--vanilla", hook), input = json, stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE) } # can the hook's own R session load jsonlite? 0 means yes system2(rscript, c("--vanilla", "-e", shQuote("library(jsonlite)")), stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE) # a call naming a protected path: expect 2 run_hook('{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"Rscript tests/make_reference.R"}}') # a harmless call: expect 0 run_hook('{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"Rscript scripts/05_analysis.R"}}') ``` ::: Any result other than 2 for the first call and 0 for the second means the hook is broken and is silently allowing everything. Now repeat the request from step 4 of Exercise 2. The R code mentions `data/raw`, so the guard should deny it before you see an approval prompt. To see exactly what each tool sends to hooks, temporarily add a `PostToolUse` hook with no matcher that appends its input to a log file (Posit Assistant's hooks documentation gives an example), and read the log. :::: ::: ::::: :::::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Break your own guard :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Red-team the tripwire :::: ::::{.task-container} The live block removed the scratch file at the end. Recreate it first, in the R console, and commit it from the Git pane: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} writeLines("a", here::here("data", "raw", "scratch.csv")) ``` ::: **Prompt (Claude Code):** ```text Run this R code: writeLines(c("a", "test"), here::here("data", "raw", "scratch.csv")) ``` The guard searches for the text `data/raw`. This call never contains it, because `here::here()` assembles the path from separate pieces, so the guard allows the call. A Windows path written with backslashes would also slip past. This is the general limit of hooks that match text: they catch the obvious form of a dangerous action, not every way of expressing it. Claude Code's documentation makes the same point about command patterns. A guard hook is a tripwire that stops accidents and makes intent visible; it is not a wall. The Git pane still shows the change. Revert the file there before moving on. :::: ::: **Your guard hook depends on jsonlite, which is not installed. What happens when the agent tries to edit a protected file?**
::::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## The review gate on GitHub Local controls do not exist for an agent that works remotely, such as the Copilot cloud agent. There, the controls are on the repository itself. Neither file below is in the workshop template; you create them. **1. CODEOWNERS.** Create `.github/CODEOWNERS` on your default branch: ``` /data/raw/ @your-github-username /tests/ @your-github-username /.github/ @your-github-username /hooks/ @your-github-username /.claude/ @your-github-username /.posit/ @your-github-username ``` Code owners are requested for review automatically when a pull request changes the files they own. CODEOWNERS works in public repositories on free plans; for private repositories it requires a paid plan. **2. Branch protection.** In the repository settings, add a rule for `main` that requires a pull request before merging, requires review from code owners, and requires the `r-checks` status check to pass. The `r-checks` workflow is set up in the *Going further* section of [Block 9](11i-characterisation-tests.qmd). **3. Test it.** Open a pull request that changes a file under `tests/`, for example by asking the Copilot cloud agent to "update the test to use a tolerance of 1e-6". Confirm that the pull request cannot merge until you have reviewed it. GitHub does not let you approve your own pull request. In a repository where you are the only person, a pull request you open yourself may need an administrator override, which is a reason to test this gate with an agent's pull request. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Feedback hooks: useful, with a warning Hooks can do more than block. A `PostToolUse` hook can run `lintr` on each R file the agent edits and pass the result back to it. A `Stop` hook can run the test suite and refuse to let the agent finish while tests fail. The second is powerful and dangerous: an agent told it cannot stop until tests pass may try to change the tests. Use it only when the deny rules and guard hook protect `tests/`. ::: ## Glossary ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
term definition
branch protection GitHub repository settings that stop changes reaching a branch such as main unless conditions are met, for example a passing check and an approved review.
checksum A short fingerprint computed from a file's contents, for example with tools::md5sum(). Any change to the file changes the checksum, so it detects changes made by any route.
CODEOWNERS A GitHub file listing who must review changes to which paths. With branch protection, a pull request that touches those paths cannot merge without their review.
deny rule A permission rule in the deny list of .claude/settings.json that stops Claude Code's built-in tools from editing or reading the matching files. It checks shell output redirects such as > file, but not R code or most other commands that change the same files.
hook A command the assistant runs automatically at a fixed point, for example before every tool call. A hook can block the call, but it matches text, so a differently written command can get past it.
instruction file A file the assistant loads into every conversation, such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, stating the project's standing conventions. Its contents are requests, not guarantees.
tool call A single action an agent takes, such as reading a file, editing a file or running a shell command. Permission rules and hooks act on tool calls.
````` ::: ::: ## References - Claude Code documentation: *Configure permissions*, ; *Hooks reference*, ; *Extend Claude Code*, . - Posit Assistant documentation: *Permissions & Trust*, ; *Hooks*, . - GitHub documentation: *About code owners*, .
